newsitem.title: GERMANY: Compaq hones strategy after German slowdown.
newsitem.headline: Compaq hones strategy after German slowdown.

text.p: Compaq Computer Corp., the world's largest personal computer maker, plans to unveil a strategy this week to shore up stalled growth in Germany, Europe's largest PC market.
Although Compaq posted healthy growth across Europe last year and worldwide sales boomed, its sales and market share in Germany declined, according to market researcher Dataquest in London.
Chief executive Eckhard Pfeiffer will detail a new German strategy as part of his company's annual news conference in Munich on Friday, spokesman Ullrich Esser told Reuters.
"It was a difficult year. We didn't have strong growth as we did the year before," he said. "At the press conference we will say what we are doing about it in Germany."
Esser declined to outline the strategy ahead of the news conference.
Compaq sales in 1996 rose 6.9 percent across Europe, but fell 10 percent in Germany in the face of stiff price competition from local PC makers and weak demand, said Dataquest analyst Chris Jones.
Its market share in Germany fell two points to 7.8 percent, while it remained Europe's leader with 12.6 percent, he said.
Siemens Nixdorf Informationssysteme AG (SNI), retailer Vobis Microcomputer AG and Fujitsu regularly beat Compaq on price last year, Jones said.
Compaq also lost momentum in the portable computer segment because of the transition to its new Armada line, he said.
"They have the complete range of products but they are struggling in Germany," Jones said. "They suffer because they have not been able to compete with SNI on large deals."
Esser said Compaq's sales to small and mid-sized companies were growing strongly, but declined to detail its German results until the news conference.
Compaq's home PC sales were flat in 1996, hurt by both stiff competition and Germany's sluggish economy, according to Dataquest.
Compaq last month said it expected strong growth in 1997 group sales after worldwide revenue rose 23 percent to $18.1 billion and net income increased 66 percent to $1.3 billion.
The company said it was in a "very good position to expand market share and increase profit."
